WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You'll help shape how ARQ manages security governance, risk and compliance across the group. Based in Colombia, you'll work directly with our group CISO and a global security team, owning programmes that support our growth across multiple markets.

We're looking for someone who takes ownership beyond preparing for an audit. You'll turn framework requirements into practical controls, work with engineers to close gaps, and give partners, auditors and regulators a clear picture of how we manage security. You'll also help us automate repetitive work, from evidence collection and questionnaires to vendor reviews.

This is an individual contributor role with broad ownership and a path towards leading GRC as the function grows.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own and improve security compliance programmes, including SOC 2, PCI DSS readiness and GDPR-related requirements.

 - Coordinate audit preparation and delivery: define scope, work with control owners, maintain evidence and drive findings through to remediation.

 - Own the vendor security due diligence programme, from initial risk assessment and security reviews to ongoing monitoring and reassessment.

 - Lead responses to security questionnaires, partner audits and regulatory requests, working with regional stakeholders and the group security team.

 - Keep the security risk register, policies and procedures current, with clear owners and actionable remediation plans.

 - Own privacy work across the group, partnering with relevant teams on data processing agreements, international transfers and breach notification requirements.

 - Translate security and compliance obligations into concrete tasks for engineering and business teams.

 - Help build automated workflows and AI-assisted processes that reduce repetitive GRC work while maintaining evidence quality and human oversight.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 5+ years in information security GRC, IT audit or cyber risk, including at least 2 years in financial services.

 - Experience owning evidence collection and coordinating control owners through a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit, alongside working knowledge of PCI DSS.

 - A practical understanding of GDPR, including lawful basis, data processing agreements, international transfers and breach notification.

 - Experience running vendor security reviews and interpreting SOC 2 reports, including exceptions and complementary user entity controls.

 - The ability to write clear policies and procedures and turn control requirements into practical actions for engineers.

 - Experience working directly with auditors or regulators and managing findings through to closure.

 - Spanish fluency sufficient to lead discussions with regulators and auditors, alongside professional English for working with a global team.

 - The autonomy to manage priorities and drive programmes forward while working with colleagues across countries and time zones.

 - Based in Colombia, preferably Bogotá, with the right to work there.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience within an SFC-supervised entity or a fintech undergoing SFC licensing.

 - Exposure to other LatAm regulators, such as CNBV, BCRA or BCB.

 - Experience implementing ISO 27001 or supporting PCI DSS assessments.

 - Familiarity with GRC platforms such as Vanta, Drata or OneTrust.

 - Enough AWS and cloud security knowledge to assess engineering evidence and challenge gaps.

 - Experience automating GRC workflows.

 - Portuguese language skills.

 - Competitive salary and benefits

 - Stock options, so you own part of what you build

 - Discretionary performance bonus

 - The latest tools and technology

 - A world-class team that will challenge and grow your skills

 - The opportunity to help build the best fintech app in Latin America

 - Office Policy: 3-4 days a week in-office

About Meridial

Meridial places skilled, remote-first professionals into high-trust, high-precision operational opportunities for leading technology companies. Our teams work as an embedded extension of our clients' own product and operations organizations, holding the same quality bar and the same deadlines.

The Opportunity

As an SMB AI Power User on the Competitive Evaluations team, you'll help a major consumer technology company find out where its bundled AI assistant subscription falls short of the standalone assistants small businesses already pay for. You are not an AI researcher studying the problem from the outside - you are a working or experienced business owner who already runs on these tools, and your own operations are the test bed.

Your day is spent doing what you already do: drafting ad copy, planning content, answering customer messages, researching suppliers, and reconciling numbers. The difference is that you do it across competing assistants, side by side, and document precisely where each one breaks. The failures you surface are the failures real paying subscribers will hit, which is exactly why the seat calls for a genuine operator rather than an evaluator.



What You'll Do

  • Run head-to-head prompts and multi-turn workflows across the client's assistant and competing paid assistants, using tasks drawn from your own business operations and marketing.
  • Build and maintain a library of realistic small-business test cases spanning ad creative and copy, organic content planning, customer messaging, competitor research, pricing, scheduling, and light bookkeeping.
  • Identify and document failure modes - wrong answers, unnecessary refusals, weak instruction-following, tone misses, brand-unsafe output, broken formatting, context lost across turns, unusable image or video output.
  • Write clear, reproducible reports: prompt used, model and surface, expected output, actual output, severity, and why the failure matters to a paying business subscriber.
  • Assess the bundled subscription on value terms - what a business owner actually receives versus what a standalone competitor subscription delivers for comparable spend.
  • Stress-test assistant features inside the social and commerce surfaces where business owners meet them, not only the standalone chat product.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Owner or operator of a small or medium business - sole proprietor, founder, or the person running day-to-day operations at a business of roughly 1–200 employees.
  • Daily, habitual use of generative AI tools in that business, for both operations and marketing. Experimental or occasional use is not a fit.
  • Organic presence on Instagram and Facebook for the business, maintained personally: posting, Stories, Reels, comment and message response.
  • Hands-on paid advertising experience on Meta platforms - has personally built, launched, and optimized campaigns with real budget.
  • Based in the United States and authorized to work here.
  • Capacity sufficient to complete deliverables per the agreed scope and timeline, which may include up to 40 hours per week 
  • Exceptional written English - able to describe a failure clearly enough that an engineer can reproduce it without follow-up.
  • Comfortable working independently against a rubric and holding a weekly output cadence.

Nice to Have

  • At least one current paid AI subscription (ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max, Gemini Advanced, or similar), so competitive comparison rests on actual use.
  • Runs a side business or second venture alongside a primary role - the profile that tends to test AI hardest against limited time.
  • Heavy Instagram user, personally and commercially: fluent in Reels, Stories, trends, and creator tooling.
  • Subscribes to two or more AI assistants simultaneously and holds an informed view on where each one wins.
  • Uses AI beyond chat - automations, agents, API or no-code integrations, custom GPTs or Projects.
  • Prior experience with model evaluation, red teaming, data annotation, QA, or structured user research.
  • Working familiarity with adjacent SMB tooling: Shopify, Square, QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Canva, CapCut, Later, or similar.
  • Industry range across the two hires - for example, one services or retail operator alongside one e-commerce or creator-economy operator.

 

We offer a pay range of $40-$50 per hour, with the exact rate determined after evaluating your experience, expertise, and geographic location. As a contractor you’ll supply a secure computer and high‑speed internet; company‑sponsored benefits such as health insurance and PTO do not apply.

ABOUT SWEETSPOT HEATING & COOLING

SweetSpot is a growing home-services company in the New York metro, and we are building our creative team from zero. This is the number one creative seat in the company, not a slot in a large agency hierarchy. The strategist hired here owns the function, works directly with the owner, and has a real path to leading the team as we scale.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a creative strategist who will own paid ad creative end to end: research, angles, hooks, scripts, briefing creators and editors, and the learnings that turn winners into the next batch.

This is not a "make pretty ads" role and it is not strategy-only. You will direct really strong video editors and UGC creators, and you will use AI (including Claude Code) as your production engine for research, hooks, scripts and variants. We are honest about the level this role is hired at: we are looking for strong raw talent with real direct-response instincts who wants ownership and serious training, and who wants to grow into a top-tier strategist with us. You will get mentorship, a proven creative system, and weekly learnings reviews. In return we expect pace, curiosity, and work you can defend.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build the research base first: homeowner avatars, desires, objections, competitors, and our own ad account history. No angles before research.

 - Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency.

 - Write hooks and scripts built for the first 3 seconds: one desire, one avatar, one message per ad.

 - Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad.

 - Run the testing system: from one winning angle, build structured iterations where each variation tests something named.

 - Run the learnings: label every ad (Breakthrough, Spend Winner, KPI Winner, Loser), state why it performed, and turn that into the next round.

 - Hit 20 to 30 finished, launch-ready ads per month at full pace, working with our editors and AI workflows.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Direct-response ad experience: you have written ads that ran as paid social (Meta or TikTok) and you can show them.

 - A testing system, not just good taste. You can explain how you turn one winner into 20 variations.

 - Research discipline. Your hooks trace to evidence, not guesses.

 - AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your creative workflow and can show how.

 - Execution: you have briefed creators or managed editors and shipped finished ads.

 - Ownership mindset: you talk about business outcomes, not just outputs delivered, and you close feedback loops: you learn, you apply, you show what changed.

 - Local services or lead generation experience is a plus, not a requirement. Seasonal urgency, emergency calls, proof and trust are the game here.


PAY AND STRUCTURE

 - Contract (1099), remote, month-to-month: $4,000 to $8,000 per month, 40 hours per week, based on experience.

 - Performance bonus structure discussed after the trial month, tied to winning ads.

 - Growth path: this seat grows into leading the creative team. One of the paths we model is editor or strategist to team lead as spend scales.


OUR HIRING PROCESS (EXACTLY HOW IT WORKS)

 1. Short application: portfolio of ads you wrote that actually ran, plus 3 short answers (your testing system on a real winner; one ad you iterated and what it tested; your AI workflow).

 2. Interview 1 (30 minutes): screening and craft in one call, run as a working session on your past ads: what did you learn, how did you apply it, what feedback loops did you complete.

 3. Paid test: $100 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours of work, paid regardless of outcome. A short research snapshot, hooks, scripts, an iteration plan and an execution plan for a real scenario.

 4. Interview 2 (final, with the owner): we walk your test together and you defend your choices. References are checked after this call (we will ask to speak with one past employer). Two interviews total, no more.

 5. Paid 30-day trial at your full agreed monthly rate, with daily contact, mentorship and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.

We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview. If you are the kind of strategist who would rather prove it than pitch it, apply.

Tempo is seeking a highly motivated and skilled Engineering Technician with strong welding capabilities to produce engineered parts and assemble testing apparatus, instruments, sensors, prototypes, and power electronic components. You will work both independently and collaboratively to bring our engineering designs to life. This role is integral to the development and refinement of high-temperature energy storage components, offering an incredible opportunity to work on complex R&D projects and grow your career at the cutting edge of thermochemical energy storage technology.

Key Responsibilities

  • Interpret 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and spec charts to plan and execute part manufacturing; measure, mark, and cut raw materials accordingly
  • Perform TIG/MIG welding on structural assemblies and operate machine shop equipment (mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws) to create or modify parts
  • Assist in assembling complex mechanical and electromechanical systems as required
  • Prepare finished components for dimensional accuracy, weld integrity, and defects for inspection
  • Modify and repair parts, prototypes, and test rigs to support agile R&D needs using welding, grinding, cutting, and machining techniques
  • Work with high-temperature and specialty materials (refractory metals, ceramics, alloys) to meet durability and performance requirements for thermochemical applications
  • Partner with engineers to interpret technical drawings, troubleshoot fabrication challenges, and recommend design improvements for manufacturability
  • Inspect fabricated and welded components for structural integrity, finish, and dimensional accuracy to ensure parts meet required tolerances
  • Maintain welding gear and machine tools in optimal working condition; follow all safety protocols when welding, handling high-temperature materials, and operating machinery
  • Record prototype builds, assembly procedures, fabrication parameters, and component modifications, providing real-time feedback to engineering and R&D teams

Qualifications
Required:

  • Associate degree in Mechanical Engineering Technology, formal welding certification, or completion of a technical/trade school program
  • 2–4 years of hands-on experience in mechanical fabrication, welding, and assembly; experience in an R&D or startup environment a plus
  • Proficiency in TIG and MIG welding on various metals
  • Exceptional safety acumen and commitment to safe work practices
  • Familiarity with manual mills, lathes, grinders, and general metalworking tools
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, and technical specifications
  • Strong willingness to learn about high-temperature and specialty materials (ceramics, alloys, refractory metals) 
  • Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to work to tight tolerances
  • Proactive learner with the ability to assist in troubleshooting basic fabrication challenges.
  • Clear communicator able to collaborate effectively with engineers and team members in a fast-paced R&D environment
  • Genuine interest in learning and growing within an R&D or startup environment; comfortable wearing multiple hats to get the job done

Preferred:

  • Experience in high-temperature applications, thermal systems, or energy storage
  • Knowledge of materials science, particularly around fabrication and welding of heat-resistant materials
  • Familiarity with safety standards and best practices in fabrication and high-temperature R&D settings

Compensation Range

Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, location, and relevant education or training. 

Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity or benefits.

Tempo is a lean organization working on exciting challenges, and the people who thrive here share a few things in common beyond their technical skills.

  • Low-ego helpfulness: You're willing to jump in on work that isn't strictly yours, whether that's helping a teammate debug something, lending a hand in the shop, or flagging an issue you noticed outside your lane. No one here succeeds in a silo.
  • Intellectual curiosity: You're genuinely interested in how things work, not just your piece of it, but the broader system. Tempo sits at the intersection of chemistry, mechanical engineering, power electronics, and software; the more you understand about the whole, the more valuable you become.
  • Business awareness: You understand that your work exists in a business context. You think about cost, timeline, and tradeoffs—not just technical elegance—and you make decisions accordingly.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: Processes here are still being built. You can make progress without a perfect playbook, and you know when to ask for direction versus when to use your judgment and move forward.
  • Accountability: You own your outcomes, including the misses. When something goes sideways, the instinct here is to fix it and learn from it, not to explain why it wasn't your fault.

Tempo is seeking a motivated, hands-on Engineering Intern to support the development and experimental validation of its high-temperature thermal energy storage technology.

The intern will work primarily on the SoFuel test stand, an experimental system designed to investigate high-temperature solid pellet storage, gas-solid heat transfer, granular material flow, and thermal system performance. This position offers an opportunity to work directly with experimental hardware, operate and improve a research-scale test system, analyze test data, and contribute to the development of next-generation energy storage technology.

We are looking for someone who enjoys building, testing, troubleshooting, and solving practical engineering problems in a laboratory environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Experimental Testing and Test Stand Operation

  • Assist in preparing, setting up, and operating the SoFuel experimental test stand under the supervision of experienced engineers.
  • Execute experimental test plans to evaluate gas–solid heat transfer, particle flow behavior, and system performance.
  • Monitor operating parameters, including temperature, gas flow rate, pressure, and particle movement.
  • Conduct repeatability tests and evaluate the effects of changing operating conditions.
  • Follow established operating procedures and safety protocols during testing.

2. Instrumentation and Data Acquisition

  • Set up, calibrate, and troubleshoot sensors and measurement equipment, including thermocouples, flow meters, pressure transducers, and distance sensors.
  • Monitor and record experimental data using the test stand's data acquisition and control systems.
  • Verify data quality, identify measurement anomalies, and maintain organized experimental records.
  • Support improvements to instrumentation and data collection procedures.

3. Troubleshooting and Test Stand Improvements

  • Assist in identifying and resolving operational issues such as particle clogging, inconsistent flow, temperature fluctuations, and sensor malfunctions.
  • Support mechanical modifications, component replacement, and routine maintenance of the test stand.
  • Work with engineers to evaluate improvements to gas flow control, particle discharge mechanisms, and test stand reliability.
  • Help implement and validate improvements to operating procedures and control sequences.

4. Data Analysis and Reporting

  • Process and analyze experimental data using Excel, Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.
  • Generate plots showing temperature profiles, flow behavior, pressure changes, and system performance.
  • Compare experimental results across different operating conditions.
  • Prepare concise technical summaries, test reports, and presentations documenting results and observations.
  • Maintain accurate test logs and document experimental findings and recommended improvements.

  • Currently pursuing a BS or MS degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Strong interest in hands-on experimental engineering and laboratory testing.
  • Basic understanding of thermodynamics, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics.
  • Familiarity with laboratory instrumentation and data acquisition.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and basic engineering data analysis.
  • Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while collaborating with a multidisciplinary engineering team.
  • Good problem-solving, troubleshooting, communication, and documentation skills.
  • Willingness to work with experimental hardware in a laboratory environment and follow strict safety procedures.

  • Experience with thermocouples, pressure sensors, flow meters, valves, or data acquisition systems.
  • Familiarity with Python, Arduino C#, LabVIEW, or similar software for data processing and automation.
  • Experience with mechanical assembly, fabrication, or troubleshooting.
  • Basic understanding of control systems, programmable controllers, or automated test equipment.
  • Experience with high-temperature equipment, furnaces, granular materials, or gas–solid flow systems.
  • Familiarity with CAD software such as SolidWorks is a plus.

What You Will Gain

  • Hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting a high-temperature experimental system.
  • Practical exposure to thermal engineering, fluid mechanics, instrumentation, and control systems.

CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. About the Team

The Global Data Center Operations team serves as the backbone of our infrastructure, ensuring the seamless performance of our global hyperscale environment. Operating in a high-stakes, 24/7 setting, this team is responsible for safeguarding the availability, stability, and reliability of mission-critical systems that power our most essential services.

As a Facilities Command Center Engineer, you bring facilities engineering judgment to mission control for our global data center fleet. Where a site engineer owns one building, you see every building at once. You will conduct structured remote rounds across every site we operate using BMS, EPMS, DCIM, and every other telemetry source available to us, and when something looks wrong, you are the person who works out what it means.

Our telemetry is not always timely or clean, and not every alarm has a runbook. This role exists for those moments. You will read one-line diagrams and sequences of operation, diagnose electrical, mechanical, and fire protection events from incomplete data, decide whether and where to send people, and make sure work in the field is safe and authorized before it starts.

This is a remote engineering role performed from the Command Center. You will not be turning wrenches, but you need to understand the equipment as if you had, because the person turning the wrench is relying on your call.

Key responsibilities:
Diagnose moderate-to-high complexity issues across electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety systems using telemetry, one-line diagrams, P&IDs, sequences of operation, and equipment documentation.

  • Make the call when no runbook fits: assess risk to production, decide whether to dispatch, and direct the first response within defined limits.

  • Review work requests, MOPs, and change records submitted by site teams and vendors for safety and operational compliance before work is authorized.

  • Conduct scheduled remote rounds each shift, reviewing and recording the health of electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety systems across the fleet.

  • Monitor critical assets including UPS systems, standby generators and fuel systems, switchgear, PDUs, battery plant, chillers, CRAH/CRAC units, cooling towers, pumps, air handlers, and fire suppression systems.

  • Baseline normal operating conditions, trend performance across sites, and identify drift and early-warning signatures before they become events.

  • Serve as first responder for infrastructure alarms, triaging incidents and initiating response per SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs.

  • Escalate to on-site operations, engineering teams, and leadership based on defined escalation matrices, with a clear technical assessment attached.

  • Coordinate incident response across multiple teams and sites, and remotely support on-site technicians, vendors, and contractors during events and planned maintenance.

  • Write and correct operating procedures based on what you see across the fleet, and feed lessons learned back to site leadership.

  • Act as technical lead on root cause analysis, providing timelines, alarm histories, and an engineering read of what failed and why.

  • Coach Command Center Technicians on your crew and help them build the facilities depth to grow into this role.

  • Maintain detailed event logs and lead structured shift handovers to keep operations continuous across crews.

Work Schedule:

Our Command Center operates 24/7/365. You will be assigned to a night crew, 

  • Shift: 12.5 hours, including a 30-minute handover overlap at each end of the shift.

  • Rotation: A fixed two-week repeating pattern (2-2-3) with every other weekend off. Depending on crew assignment, you will work either:

    • Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday in week one; Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday in week two, or

    • Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday in week one; Sunday, Wednesday, Thursday in week two.

  • Cycle: Three scheduled shifts in one week and four in the next, repeating. You will never work more than four shifts in a single week.

  • Night differential: Night crew assignments are paid a 10% shift differential.

  • Holidays: The Command Center is staffed on holidays. Holiday coverage is part of the rotation.

  • Handover: Every shift begins and ends with a structured handover. Punctuality is a safety requirement, not a preference.

  • On-site presence: This role is performed from the Command Center and requires on-site presence for the duration of each shift.

This is a salaried, exempt position.

Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience operating or maintaining critical facilities: data centers, utilities and power generation, hospitals, semiconductor fabs, or industrial plants.

  • Hands-on background in electrical systems (UPS, switchgear, generators, ATS/STS, batteries) or mechanical systems (chillers, CRAH/CRAC, cooling towers, pumps, controls), with working knowledge of the other.

  • Ability to read and reason from one-line diagrams, P&IDs, and sequences of operation.

  • Proven experience writing, reviewing, and executing SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs in high-availability environments.

  • Experience making operational decisions under pressure with incomplete information, and explaining the reasoning afterward.

  • Ability to interpret telemetry, trend data, and alarm behavior to separate real risk from noise.

  • Strong written communication. Much of your work product is the written record of what happened, why, and what to change.

  • Ability and willingness to work 12.5-hour shifts on a fixed two-week rotating pattern, including weekends, holidays, and nights if assigned to a night crew.

  • Work is performed in a climate-controlled Command Center, primarily seated at a multi-monitor operator workstation.

Preferred Skills:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent military technical training (for example, Navy nuclear or marine engineering programs).

  • Experience as a data center facility engineer, critical facilities engineer, or chief engineer in a hyperscale or colocation environment.

  • Stationary engineer, electrical, or HVAC trade license.

  • Data center operations certifications such as CNet CDCTP or Uptime Institute AOS/ATD.

  • Familiarity with specific BMS, EPMS, and DCIM platforms.

  • Experience in a centralized Command Center, Facility Operations Center, or NOC supporting multiple sites.

  • Experience with root cause analysis methods and incident management frameworks.

We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams, even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk.

  • You love to understand how a system really behaves, not just what the alarm says.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

As a Solutions Engineer at Onebrief, you work where mission, engineering, and compliance meet.

You'll own technical solution design and deployment readiness, translating customer requirements into secure, scalable deployment architectures. You'll partner with Platform Engineering, SRE, and our Cybersecurity team to validate infrastructure, configure environments, resolve technical blockers, and successfully transition solutions into production.

You’ll work with our go-to-market and customer facing teams to meet with planners, operations officers, and network owners to understand how they work today. You’ll help show them what that work looks like in Onebrief, and then you'll make it real.

You connect a staff's planning problem to a live, accredited Onebrief deployment.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Core responsibilities:

 - Run technical discovery. With Sales and Engineering, map a staff's current workflow and pain points, specifically focusing on their technical constraints: networks, hosting, identity, and integration requirements, especially in multi-network environments.

 - Lead deployment engineering. Coordinate the technical delivery of new deployments, including infrastructure validation, network configuration checks, and system readiness verification. Write code to configure new deployments and support new environments.

 - Support accreditation. Help create and review security documentation, including STIG checklists and ATO artifacts, alongside our cybersecurity team so deployments are accredited on the customer's timeline.

 - Align stakeholders. Get technical stakeholders on both sides to agree on requirements, constraints, and tradeoffs, so customers see value sooner. Ensure those technical requirements are properly translated into contract deliverables.

 - Scope integrations. Design how Onebrief Connect fits into a command's ecosystem: APIs, data pipelines, Foundry and Maven Smart System, CUOPS tools, and dashboards.

 - Deliver tailored demos.  Lead technical demonstrations and solution validation, partnering with Sales and customer-facing teams to demonstrate Onebrief's technical capabilities, deployment architecture, security posture, and integration options.

 - Run pilot deployments. Configure Onebrief in new and untested environments to enable limited uses in support of new sales.

 - Turn field experience into patterns. Convert what you learn in deployments into structured workflows and reusable implementation patterns, and feed clear requirements to Product and Engineering.

 - Work with customers onsite. This is a hybrid role, requiring you to work alongside customers as necessary. 




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Secret Clearance required.

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

 - 4+ years in solutions engineering, infrastructure or deployment engineering, or forward-deployed engineering, working closely with go-to-market and operational teams

 - Experience in DoW environments and their security and compliance requirements (RMF, STIGs, ICD 503)

 - Strong expertise with containers (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)

 - Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and on-premises virtualization (RHEL)

 - Solid understanding of networking concepts and protocols, and of security best practices for highly sensitive environments

 - Strong presence with customers, from action officers to senior leaders, and clear, concise writing

 - Calm under pressure, and focused on forward motion




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Proficiency in a scripting language (Python, Go, or Bash)

 - Infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible)

 - Monitoring and logging tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Datadog) and service mesh (Istio, Linkerd)

 - Experience as a military planner or staff officer, or with mission command systems, Foundry, or Maven Smart System

 - Presales experience, including building and delivering demos
